chunks.title: How to Make a Property Listing Video in South Africa — How to Make a Property Listing Video in South Africa
chunks.text: How to Make a Property Listing Video in South Africa. South African buyers scroll before they call. Whether a listing lands on Property24, Instagram or a WhatsApp status, the agents who show motion first get the viewings. The good news: a professional-looking listing video no longer needs a camera crew or an editor — just a phone, your existing photos, and about ten minutes.

chunks.title: How to Make a Property Listing Video in South Africa — The 60-second listing video formula
chunks.text: The 60-second listing video formula. Every strong property video follows the same beats, regardless of price bracket: Hook (0–3s): the best angle of the property, with suburb and price on screen. If you lose people here, you lose the viewing.. Walkthrough (3–40s): flow room to room the way a visitor would experience it — entrance, living areas, kitchen, main bedroom, garden or view.. Details (40–50s): beds, baths, erf size, solar or inverter, security, proximity to schools and the highway.. Call to action (50–60s): your name, agency, and "Book a viewing" — plus a link you can paste into WhatsApp.

chunks.title: How to Make a Property Listing Video in South Africa — What to shoot (or fake) with a phone
chunks.text: What to shoot (or fake) with a phone. Landscape for portals, portrait for socials. Shoot or crop both — a 16:9 cut for the listing page and a 9:16 cut for WhatsApp status, Reels and TikTok.. Shoot in the morning or late afternoon. Midday Highveld sun flattens interiors; golden hour flatters Cape and KZN coastlines.. Steady beats fancy. Walk slowly, hold the phone with two hands, and let rooms breathe for two seconds before panning.. No loadshedding? Still check the lights. Film with every globe working; a dead downlight reads as a defect.

chunks.title: How to Make a Property Listing Video in South Africa — What does a listing video cost in South Africa?
chunks.text: What does a listing video cost in South Africa?. Three options, three budgets: Videographer on site: roughly R1 500–R5 000 per property depending on location and edits — worth it for R5m+ listings, hard to justify for every new instruction.. DIY on a phone: free, but the editing time is real — most agents underestimate it at 2–4 hours per listing.. AI from your existing photos: upload the photos you already took, pick a tier and voice, and get a narrated reel back in minutes. On PropReel pricing this works out to a few rand per video in credits — create a free account and you start with 5 free credits.

chunks.text: Formats portals and social platforms actually accept. Property24 / Private Property: 16:9 MP4, keep it under a minute for the listing embed; a YouTube link also works.. Instagram Reels & TikTok: 9:16, 15–45 seconds, captions burned in — most viewers watch muted at first.. WhatsApp status: 9:16, under 30 seconds, smallest file you can send without quality collapsing.. Email to your database: link the video, don’t attach it — attachments get stripped by corporate mail filters.

chunks.title: Social Media Marketing for Estate Agents: A South African Playbook — Social Media Marketing for Estate Agents: A South African Playbook
chunks.text: Social Media Marketing for Estate Agents: A South African Playbook. Most agents post when they remember: a photo of a new listing, nothing for two weeks, then three posts in one day. Consistency beats intensity in property marketing, and one listing can feed every platform you use. Here is a playbook that fits around viewings instead of eating them.

chunks.title: Social Media Marketing for Estate Agents: A South African Playbook — Where South African buyers actually are
chunks.text: Where South African buyers actually are. Facebook: still the widest reach for family homes and the home of suburb and community groups. Buy-and-sell groups move stock fast in every metro.. Instagram: the showcase. Reels of new listings, before/after staging, and "sold in X days" posts build your personal brand with aspirational buyers.. TikTok: the discovery engine — one property tour can reach people who were not even looking yet. Cheap to make, expensive to over-produce.. LinkedIn: the right channel for commercial property, investor stock and referral relationships with brokers and attorneys.. WhatsApp: not a broadcast channel — a conversion channel. More on that in how to market property on WhatsApp.

chunks.title: Social Media Marketing for Estate Agents: A South African Playbook — Turn one listing into five posts
chunks.text: Turn one listing into five posts. The bottleneck is not posting — it is content. One new instruction should yield: The announcement: hero photo or 30-second video, price, suburb, key hook ("walking distance to the station").. The tour: a narrated video walkthrough — render it from your listing photos with PropReel in minutes.. The detail post: one feature done well — the kitchen island, the solar setup, the sea view — with a carousel.. The neighbourhood post: schools, coffee spots, commute times. This is what gets shared into community groups.. The social proof: "Just listed", "Multiple offers", "Sold at asking" — momentum posts make your phone ring.

chunks.title: Social Media Marketing for Estate Agents: A South African Playbook — A cadence you can keep
chunks.text: A cadence you can keep. Three posts a week minimum on your main channel — two listings-driven, one personality or market commentary.. Daily stories when you have them: arrived at a viewing, inside a new instruction, sold. Stories are for presence, feed posts for reach.. One long-form item a month: a suburb market update or price-band analysis. It compounds in search and doubles as email content.

chunks.title: Social Media Marketing for Estate Agents: A South African Playbook — Measure what pays
chunks.text: Measure what pays. Ignore vanity metrics. Track three things monthly: direct messages from posts, viewing requests attributed to a specific listing post, and how many enquiries mention seeing "the video". If a format never produces one of those three after a month, stop making it. The fastest way to raise your posting floor: attach a video to every listing. See the pricing — from R1.50 per credit, no subscription required.

chunks.title: How to Market Property Listings on WhatsApp (Without Being Blocked) — How to Market Property Listings on WhatsApp (Without Being Blocked)
chunks.text: How to Market Property Listings on WhatsApp (Without Being Blocked). WhatsApp is South Africa’s real social network — and every agent knows it. It is also the fastest way to get muted, reported or blocked. The difference between the two outcomes is format, frequency and usefulness. Here is how to use WhatsApp as a marketing channel that buyers welcome.

chunks.title: How to Market Property Listings on WhatsApp (Without Being Blocked) — Status: your free billboard
chunks.text: Status: your free billboard. One listing per status, morning and evening. Status expires in 24 hours; staggering beats a burst of eight.. Video rules: 9:16 portrait, under 30 seconds, keep the file small — WhatsApp recompresses aggressively, so a crisp short clip survives better than a long one.. Text + link status: photo from the listing, price in the caption, link to the full video or listing page. The link is what converts.. Personalise the first line: "Morning team — new listing in Bryanston" reads differently from a forwarded blast.

chunks.title: How to Market Property Listings on WhatsApp (Without Being Blocked) — Groups: give value before you sell
chunks.text: Groups: give value before you sell. Join suburb and buy/sell groups as a resident, not an advertiser. Comment helpfully first; post listings when the group culture allows it.. One post per new instruction per group — never the same wording five times a day. Repetition is what gets you reported.. Answer questions publicly. "What goes for R2.5m in that area?" is a listing opportunity disguised as a favour.

chunks.title: How to Market Property Listings on WhatsApp (Without Being Blocked) — Broadcast lists and WhatsApp Business
chunks.text: Broadcast lists and WhatsApp Business. Build opted-in lists — buyers who said "keep me posted" — and broadcast weekly, not daily.. WhatsApp Business catalog: load each listing with price, address and link so your profile doubles as a shopfront.. Label your contacts (hot buyer, landlord, investor) so the right broadcast goes to the right slice instead of everyone.

chunks.title: How to Market Property Listings on WhatsApp (Without Being Blocked) — Share the video, not the file
chunks.text: Share the video, not the file. A 200 MB video attachment dies in sending: compression blurs it, and some recipients never download it. Share a link instead — your PropReel render has a shareable link that opens in any browser, stays sharp, and lets you see it was opened.

chunks.title: How to Market Property Listings on WhatsApp (Without Being Blocked) — The two-minute rule
chunks.text: The two-minute rule. If a buyer would not forward your message to a friend looking for property, do not send it. Useful, sharp, rare — that is the whole strategy. Ready to make something worth forwarding? Create your first property video free — then put the link in your next status.

chunks.title: Virtual Staging in South Africa: Costs, Rules and Results — Virtual Staging in South Africa: Costs, Rules and Results
chunks.text: Virtual Staging in South Africa: Costs, Rules and Results. An empty home photographs like a promise nobody kept. Physical staging solves it — at R8 000 to R30 000+ per room-set per month for a professional crew. Virtual staging places photoreal furniture into your photos for a fraction of that, which is why SA agencies increasingly use it for show houses, off-plan units and stock that has already been handed over.

chunks.title: Virtual Staging in South Africa: Costs, Rules and Results — Virtual vs physical staging
chunks.text: Virtual vs physical staging. Cost: physical staging is a monthly rental plus delivery, styling and collection; virtual staging is a once-off per-photo cost — on PropReel it is charged in credits at R1,5 each.. Speed: virtual results land in minutes; physical staging books days or weeks ahead.. What it is for: physical staging helps buyers *feel* a home during an in-person viewing. Virtual staging helps them *click* on the listing in the first place.. Honest caveat: virtual staging cannot furnish a viewing. Budget it as a marketing layer, not a substitute for a well-presented show day.

chunks.title: Virtual Staging in South Africa: Costs, Rules and Results — Disclosure: the line you must not cross
chunks.text: Disclosure: the line you must not cross. Staged images that misrepresent room size, structure or included furniture are a complaint waiting to happen — and portals expect disclosure. The safe pattern: Label staged photos plainly: "Virtual staging" in the caption or on the image.. Never remove or add structural elements — no fake windows, no erased cracks, no extended erf.. Always keep one unstaged photo of each room in the set.. Disclose inclusions separately: what stays with the property goes in the written description, not the pixels.

chunks.title: Virtual Staging in South Africa: Costs, Rules and Results — Getting results that do not look staged
chunks.text: Getting results that do not look staged. Match the market: contemporary furniture for new developments, warmer family settings for established suburbs; coastal properties want light woods and linen.. Mind the perspective: furniture must sit correctly on the floor plane — badly anchored sofas kill trust instantly.. Declutter first, stage second: virtual staging layered over a messy room just produces a tidy mess.. Keep the light: the furniture must inherit the photo’s lighting direction, or the eye immediately knows something is off.

chunks.title: Virtual Staging in South Africa: Costs, Rules and Results — Try it on a real listing
chunks.text: Try it on a real listing. Upload an empty-room photo, pick a style, and compare before/after in under a minute — it is one of the studio tools inside PropReel’s free account. Pair the staged set with a narrated video and your listing has both the click and the story.

chunks.text: Do Listing Videos Really Sell Homes Faster? The Case for Property Video. Photo galleries tell buyers a property exists. Video lets them rehearse living in it. That difference — between awareness and imagination — is why listings with video consistently hold attention longer, get shared more, and attract more qualified enquiries. Here is the honest case for it.

chunks.title: Do Listing Videos Really Sell Homes Faster? The Case for Property Video — Attention is the scarce resource
chunks.text: Attention is the scarce resource. A buyer scrolling a portal gives each listing a fraction of a second before deciding. A thumbnail competes with ten thousand other thumbnails; a playing video competes with nothing. Even a fifteen-second silent loop buys you the pause in which the price, the suburb and the hook get read.

chunks.title: Do Listing Videos Really Sell Homes Faster? The Case for Property Video — Video travels further than links
chunks.text: Video travels further than links. WhatsApp forwards: a video file or link in a family group reaches the cousin who is quietly looking — link shares beat photo dumps because they invite a tap-through.. Social algorithms: Reels and TikToks get distributed to non-followers; static photo posts mostly reach people who already know you.. Email: listings with a video thumbnail see materially better click rates than image-only emails — the play button is an affordance.

chunks.title: Do Listing Videos Really Sell Homes Faster? The Case for Property Video — The showing-filtering effect
chunks.text: The showing-filtering effect. A thorough video pre-qualifies. Buyers who arrive having "walked" the property arrive with real questions — financing, occupation dates, offers — instead of discovering the layout mismatch in person. Fewer wasted Sunday showings, faster offers on the listings that fit.

chunks.title: Do Listing Videos Really Sell Homes Faster? The Case for Property Video — What it costs to skip video
chunks.text: What it costs to skip video. Every week on market costs money: price psychology, seller patience, and your own pipeline. If video shortens days-on-market by even a little across your stock, the maths dwarfs the production cost — and when that cost is a few rand of credits instead of a videographer, the argument barely survives contact with a calculator.

chunks.text: . # PropReel Documentation The current architecture in one paragraph: a React + Vite + Tailwind frontend and Vercel serverless TypeScript functions in api/ (12-function Hobby cap — extend existing functions rather than adding new ones). Data lives in our storage today, behind a driver switch in lib/db.ts that can move it to Supabase Postgres without touching a single API route. Supabase Auth handles sign-in, the service S3 stores every file, Modal + the render service render video, and Paystack takes payments.

chunks.title: README: Removed architecture (historical)
chunks.text: Removed architecture (historical). An earlier attempt built the product as an Express + Prisma + PostgreSQL monorepo (legacy-monorepo/) and shipped a shell-script deployment package (deploy/, deploy.sh) targeting cPanel. Both were abandoned and have been removed: Vercel serverless is the only backend, and its scripts contradicted the live data layer (they prescribed a different Postgres schema, which is what previously left conflicting tables in the Supabase project).

chunks.text: . # Spec — 1 credit per voiceover Translate Status: implemented (2026-10-27) — 1 credit per translate, first 3 free on a running trial · Owner cost: ~$0.0005–0.002 per call · Price: 1 credit (R1.50)

chunks.title: translate-credit-spec: Why
chunks.text: Why. The mismatch gate's Translate action is the last per-user LLM call that spends the owner's money without recovering anything. The volume cuts (verdict cache, check-on-settle, rate limit) made the *checks* nearly free — translation is deliberately excluded from caching because every script is unique. At 1,000 users, unlimited free translation is an open-ended LLM bill; a 1-credit charge makes every translate margin-positive (≈5–150× cost) while staying trivially cheap for the user.

chunks.title: translate-credit-spec: Pricing decision
chunks.text: Pricing decision. | Item | Value | Alternatives considered: per-word pricing (rejects — translate cost barely scales with length and per-word pricing reads as expensive), 2 credits (aligns with Social Post but "small" means small). first-N-free shipped as the trial allowance below (2026-10-27): 3 free translates on a running trial, counted off the ledger — no separate counter state.

chunks.title: translate-credit-spec: Charge lifecycle
chunks.text: Charge lifecycle. Mirrors the Social Post pattern ("2 credits per post render, refunded on failure"): 1. User clicks Translate (1 credit) in the mismatch dialog/banner. 2. POST /api/credits?action=deduct { user_id, amount: 1, reason: 'Translate voiceover script', metadata: { kind: 'TRANSLATE' } }. The server rejects any amount ≠ TRANSLATE_CREDITS (400) — the client never chooses the price. Trial freebie: while the trial is running and fewer than 3 translates are used, this step consumes one for free — it records a 0-amount kind: TRANSLATE consumption row and answers { success, free: true, free_remaining } without touching the balance. GET /api/credits?action=translate_quote reports the same numbers so the button can show "free — N left" or "1 credit" before the click. 3. 402 / insufficient balance → stop here. No LLM call happens; show the existing low-credit nudge with the top-up route. 4. On deduct success → PropReelAPI.generateText('translate', …) (unchanged). 5. Success → done; the ledger row (kind: TRANSLATE) feeds usage reporting. 6. Failure / empty response / timeout → POST /api/credits?action=refund { user_id, scope: 'translate' } and surface the error in the banner. The refund matcher reverses exactly one real unreversed deduction, so a double refund is impossible even if the client retries the call. For a trial freebie the reversal is a no-op on the balance (abs(0)) that simply un-counts the consumption row — the free try comes back instead of burning on a call that produced nothing. Retry after failure re-enters at step 2 (a fresh charge), which is correct: the f

chunks.title: translate-credit-spec: Server changes
chunks.text: Server changes. 1. lib/renderPricing.ts — add TRANSLATE_CREDITS = 1 next to DESCRIPTION_CREDITS / SOCIAL_POST_CREDITS, and extend jobCredits() with 'translate': TRANSLATE_CREDITS. 2. api/credits.ts (?action=deduct) — add || kind === 'TRANSLATE' to the server-priced-kinds branch (line ~157) and price it via jobCredits('translate'). Everything else in the handler is unchanged. 3. lib/userService.ts — add a translate entry to REFUND_MATCHERS (matches ledger rows with metadata.kind === 'TRANSLATE'); it flows into REFUND_SCOPES automatically. refundDeduction's candidate filter also accepts the 0-amount trial-free rows for this scope only (their reversal mints nothing — it exists to return the allowance). 3b. api/credits.ts — the trial allowance: translateTrialUsage() counts unreversed kind: TRANSLATE rows; ?action=translate_quote prices the next click for the UI; the deduct branch consumes a freebie (0-amount row) while isTrialRunning and usage < 3, and rejects pool: 'agency' (personal balance only).

chunks.title: translate-credit-spec: Frontend changes
chunks.text: Frontend changes. 4. src/lib/useVoiceoverLanguageCheck.ts — translate() becomes: deduct → generateText → refund-on-failure (the verdict-cache seeding on success is kept). A 402/INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS deduct maps to the low-credit message before any LLM call happens. The hook also prefetches translate_quote (deduped module cache) and exposes translateCostLabel. 5. src/components/LanguageMismatchBanner.tsx + the ConfirmContext dialog copy — button labels read "Translate to X (1 credit)" or "Translate to X (free — N left)" so the cost is visible *before* the click (the dialog already offers Translate / Keep as is; only the label changes).

chunks.title: translate-credit-spec: Edge cases
chunks.text: Edge cases. - Tampered client: sending amount: 0 or amount: 5 gets a 400 — same guarantee as Description/Social today. • Concurrent tabs: each translate charges once; refunds reverse the oldest unreversed TRANSLATE deduction (matcher semantics) — fine at 1 credit. • Concurrent tabs (trial freebies): two simultaneous clicks can both see the last free try and both go free — 1-credit exposure, same tolerance the concurrent-tabs row below already accepts. • Rate limits stay: the worker's per-user cap remains the abuse guard; credits are the monetization layer. They compose, they don't replace. • Admins: no exemption (admins can grant themselves credits via the existing admin add action); avoids a role branch in billing.

chunks.title: translate-credit-spec: Phase 2 (optional hardening)
chunks.text: Phase 2 (optional hardening). Enforcement is mint-side, matching Description today: a user who calls the worker endpoint directly with their own worker token skips the credit (cost exposure ≈ fractions of a cent per call, bounded by the rate limit). If that ever matters, mint a single-use scoped token per translate (the job_token machinery + extraHeaders already support this, same as video_script) and have /generate_text claim it for kind: 'translate'.

chunks.title: translate-credit-spec: Verification
chunks.text: Verification. - Deduct with wrong amount → 400 (table-driven over 0, 2, 0.5). • Deduct → forced LLM failure → refund lands; balance restored; second refund call returns 0 refunded. • 402 on empty balance → no LLM call (assert via stub), low-credit UI shown. • Live: mismatch dialog → Translate → 1 credit deducted, script rewritten in the target language, ledger row visible in billing history.

chunks.title: Voiceover step (step 5): the script, the word budget and AI Write
chunks.text: Voiceover step (Video Generator step 5) — the script. Narration is optional: the Narrator toggle at the top switches it off and the reel renders with music only, and your script and language stay in place for AI Write and the AI Avatar tab. The script box carries a live word budget sized to the video's duration at roughly 2.4 words per second — 30s about 72 words, 60s about 144 words, 90s about 216 words. The counter under the box says how many words are left and turns amber in the last 12 words and red once you are over. Going over never cuts your narration: the clip plays it in full and the final frame holds for a few seconds so the voiceover can finish, but trimming to the number the counter names gives a clean ending. AI Write drafts the script from your Listing details and the photos you uploaded, sized to the duration you picked. It costs 30s = 1, 60s = 2, 90s = 3 credits (1 per 30 seconds, capped at 6) and asks you to confirm the price before it runs. Clear empties the box.

chunks.title: Voiceover step: choosing the language and narrator voice, and the mismatch warning
chunks.text: Voiceover step (step 5) — language and voice. Choose the Voiceover Language first: the Narrator list underneath only ever offers voices that natively speak that language, and changing the language re-picks the first voice for it. Each narrated render is charged 1 credit for the narration, shown on the badge beside the Narrator label. The play button beside the list speaks a short sample in the chosen voice and language, and previewing is free. As you type, the step checks whether the script is written in the selected language. On a mismatch it shows a banner offering to translate the script into that language — the banner states the price before you accept — or to keep it as is. Nothing renders while the mismatch is unresolved, because a voice cannot read a language it does not speak and the narration would come out mangled. If the narration runs longer than the tier's duration, the step also warns how many seconds the last frame will hold. The script, language and voice are shared with the AI Avatar Video tab, so what you choose here is what the avatar speaks.

chunks.title: AI Avatar Video tab: what it makes and the photo it needs
chunks.text: AI Avatar Video tab — what it makes. It renders a lip-synced talking-head video of you from one headshot plus a narration script, in any of South Africa's 11 official languages. Reach it from the Avatar tab in the dashboard, or as the optional AI Avatar add-on on step 6 of the Video Generator. The photo: one face, centred, head and shoulders, evenly lit. A 1080 × 1080 square is ideal, and the finished clip is square too, so a square photo maps onto it with no cropping. The minimum is 700 px on the short side — 720 × 720 is the practical floor; a landscape photo more than about 10% wider than it is tall is centre-cropped, which can cut straight through the face. JPEG or PNG up to 25 MB. "Use my branding profile image" reuses the photo from Agent Branding instead of uploading one. The photo is shared with the Video tab, so removing it in one place removes it in the other. As soon as you pick a photo the tab measures it and warns with its real dimensions if it is too small or too wide. The script box arrives pre-filled with the Video tab's AI script and stays in sync in both directions. The avatar speaks the script exactly as written — there is no auto-translation.

chunks.title: AI Avatar Video: price per second, the 90-second cap, and what blocks Generate
chunks.text: AI Avatar Video — price and limits. Billing is 2 credits per 10 seconds of narration, minimum 2 credits, with a hard 90-second cap (about 216 words). A script past the cap is refused before anything is charged, and the tab says how long your script actually is. The Generate button carries the exact price for your script and the line beneath it shows your balance. Credits are charged when the render starts; cancelling during the render refunds them, and a failed render is refunded automatically. Generate stays blocked — with the reason spelled out under the button — until there is a photo, a non-empty script, enough credits, a script under the cap, and no unresolved script-vs-language mismatch. The result: the avatar clip renders first, then it is placed in the top-left corner of the reel and its voiceover replaces the reel's own narration. A progress bar tracks elapsed time against a typical render, and the finished clip is stored for 30 days, so download it if you want to keep it.

chunks.title: Photos step tags: "Photo is from a", "Camera move" and "Day to Twilight"
chunks.text: Photos step tags. On the AI tiers every uploaded photo gets three tags under its thumbnail. The Essential tier hides them, because it renders from the photos without AI motion, and the Budget Video wizard shows the same three tags. "Photo is from a" means Interior or Exterior — which way the photo was taken. It tells the renderer what it is looking at, and it sets the camera moves on offer for that photo. "Camera move" is how the camera behaves inside that photo's clip: Zoom in pushes forward into the property, Left sweeps in a wide arc to the left, Right sweeps to the right, and Zoom out pulls back. Zoom out is offered on Exterior photos only — retreating out of an interior would exit the room — and switching a photo between Interior and Exterior resets its move to Zoom in, which is the default for every photo. "Day to Twilight" is the light journey for that clip. "Day → Night" (the default) drifts from golden hour into dusk, so the windows glow warm by the end of the clip; "Daylight only" holds steady daylight for the whole clip, with no golden hour and no dusk. The three tags are what the per-photo render instructions are built from, so the AI tiers ask you to set them before Next; the Budget wizard defaults every photo to Interior, Zoom in and Day → Night.

chunks.title: The render finished: review every clip, then create the final video
chunks.text: When a render finishes on an AI tier, nothing is stitched yet. The Render step pauses with every generated clip listed and a panel headed "Review each clip before the final video is stitched" — the note under it says plainly that the final video only starts once you create it. Watch each clip in its own player. Under it the footer reads "Clip N of M" with the clip's current camera move, and clips that have already been replaced are marked "re-rolled". When you are happy with all of them, press "Create final video (N clips)". Assembly is free: the tier price you already paid covers narration, music, branding, the avatar if you added one, the endcard and the thumbnail, so stitching the reviewed clips costs nothing extra. If the whole set is wrong, press "Cancel render — unused credits come back" instead: the render charge is refunded and no video is produced. The Essential tier never pauses here — it renders the whole reel in one local pass, so there are no clips to review.

chunks.title: How to change one rendered clip: pick a new camera move or Day to Twilight, then re-roll it
chunks.text: Changing one clip after the render. Each clip card in the review panel carries two rows of buttons under its player. Camera move offers Zoom in, Left and Right, plus Zoom out on clips tagged Exterior — the same moves the Photos step offered, for this clip alone. Day to Twilight offers "Day → Night" and "Daylight only". Tap the move or light you want: the button highlights to show it is selected but nothing renders yet. The re-roll button at the bottom right of the card changes from "Re-roll" to "Re-roll with changes" and shows its price, and a "reset" link appears so you can drop the change and keep the clip's current move and light. Press "Re-roll with changes" to regenerate only that clip with the new instruction; the card shows "Re-rolling…" and the other clips are untouched. Press "Re-roll" without picking anything to get a fresh attempt at the exact same shot — that is the fix for artefacts like an invented room, a warped wall or fire where there should be none, because a new attempt is a new generation. The price is that clip's share of the tier: the tier's credit price divided by its photo count, rounded up — a 6-photo Social 30-second reel is 34 credits, so one clip is 6 credits — and the button always shows the exact amount before you commit. A failed re-roll keeps the original clip and refunds the charge. Only one re-roll runs at a time, and you cannot create the final video while a re-roll is still in flight.

chunks.title: Day to Twilight in the Photo Editor: converting a daytime exterior to dusk
chunks.text: Day to Twilight in the Photo Editor is a different tool from the Photos-step tag of the same name. The Photos-step tag changes how a clip's light drifts while the reel renders; the Photo Editor tab converts an existing daytime exterior photo into a dusk shot in one click, at 2 credits like every other photo edit. The presets are Blue Hour, Golden Dusk, Night Lights, Dramatic Sunset, Moody & Atmospheric, Festive Evening. Whichever you pick, the architecture stays where it is — walls, windows, roofline and landscaping keep their position and shape — and only the sky, the light and the warm window glow change. It works on exteriors, so use it on the listing's hero shot, then upload that edited image as the first photo of the reel.
